A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MMAD benchmark, dataset construction pipeline and evaluation framework. Their complete main texts, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original MLLM evaluations, template and model-scaling experiments, RAG and expert-agent comparisons, and appendix experiments on in-context learning.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds human evaluation, Claude-3.5-Sonnet results, CoT and vision-removal experiments, and additional performance diagnostics.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction pipeline and principal boost methods remain intact. v2 adds structured CoT prompting involving object identification, image comparison and defect judgment, organized into two response stages (Appendix A.3), and extends expert inputs to textual descriptions of ground-truth defect location and size (Section 4.4). v1 already used a brief analysis prompt in one qualitative example.

E1.justification: The four source datasets, 8,366 images, 39,672 questions and seven subtasks remain unchanged. Appendix A.4 adds a no-vision evaluation condition, extending testing to unavailable visual input. The human study samples existing benchmark examples rather than introducing another industrial dataset or task.

E2.justification: Table 2 extends the model-only comparison to expert and ordinary human reference groups and adds Claude-3.5-Sonnet, while retaining all previous MLLMs. The human references materially broaden the comparison underlying the industrial-inspector research question. Figure 6 also adds a GT-text comparison condition. LLaVA-OnVision becoming LLaVA-OneVision is a name correction.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include 177 randomly sampled examples assessed by three experts and five ordinary participants, structured CoT comparisons, and vision-removal controls. Appendix A.7 adds recall, precision and F1 with anomalies designated positive. These substantially extend the evaluation protocol; the original 1-shot settings and balanced anomaly-discrimination accuracy remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds systematic CoT and visual-dependence ablations, question/option vocabulary analysis, precision-recall error diagnostics, and the GT-text control. Appendix B adds human-versus-GPT-4o cases and expands the earlier cable-response example. These substantially broaden benchmark validation and failure analysis. Earlier in-context-learning results and caption/domain-knowledge cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports model-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new human sample and participant counts describe study design, without adding uncertainty estimates or repeated-run reporting.

E6.justification: All retained Table 2 scores and Tables 3–5 remain numerically unchanged. New results include Claude's 68.36% average and human averages of 86.65% and 78.69% on the sampled study. Table 6 adds CoT comparisons of 69.59% to 65.82% for InternVL2-40B and 70.75% to 72.29% for 76B. Tables 7–8 and Figure 6 add vision-removal, precision/recall/F1 and GT-text results. These are additional outcomes under specified conditions, not revisions demonstrating same-setting improvement between versions.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theorems, proofs or mathematical derivations. The additional standard evaluation metrics and positive-class convention in Appendix A.7 do not introduce substantive mathematical theory.

C1.justification: The abstract and three contribution statements retain the same benchmark, annotation-pipeline and evaluation claims. The conclusion preserves the identified industrial-knowledge and multi-image weaknesses and potential of enhancement methods. Its added statement about needing extensive data reiterates a point already made in v1's introduction.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation through explanations of CoT instability, visual dependence, missed detections versus false alarms, and contrasting human perception with GPT-4o's object knowledge. Appendix A.5 newly acknowledges that annotators may lack the originating industry's specialized expertise. Appendix A.7 also introduces an overstatement that humans outperform models on every metric, which Table 8 does not support.

D1.justification: v1 already disclosed 26 reviewers and over 200 working hours. Appendix A.5 adds reviewer expertise, preliminary program filtering, item-level review, the filtering interface, annotation cues and exclusion of erroneous questions. v2 also specifies Claude's API snapshot and describes the new prompting procedures. These are additional disclosures; the PDFs do not establish a revised dataset-construction process. The code/data access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds MathVista, Chu et al.'s CoT survey and Chen et al.'s evaluation study. It also strengthens criticism of Seed-Bench and CompBench from lacking industrial images to involving fictional tasks without realistic references. These are limited additions to the existing related-work framing.

P1.justification: v2 makes local wording corrections and condenses parts of Sections 4.1 and 4.3, while preserving the main narrative and section sequence. The appendix gains dedicated analysis subsections and moves case studies from A.3 to Appendix B. Most retained prose is unchanged, so the added scientific material does not constitute extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: The visual presentation expands substantially: Figure 1 substitutes a human curve for MiniCPM, Table 2 adds and regroups rows, and new Tables 6–8 and Figures 8–10 display ablations, filtering tools, word clouds and precision-recall results. The earlier response case is expanded with colored comparative responses, two cases are added, and older caption/domain-knowledge figures are relocated and compacted into Figures 14–17.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens benchmark validation and transparency through visual-dependence controls, error-profile metrics and clearer annotation-review documentation while preserving the original results. The net improvement is limited by the preliminary human study: only 177 examples are sampled, uncertainty is unreported, and model scores on that same subset are not clearly provided. The new claim of human superiority on every metric also contradicts Table 8, which reports higher recall for LLaVA-1.5 and higher precision for SPHINX.
